II21A-01.note: B is the reversed twin and the only real competitor. A restates the pattern the passage says fits both accounts and D contradicts it, so test-wise students strike that pair at once and are left with the reversed B/C pair.

II21A-02.note: D (pools vs backwaters, which isolates crayfish) is the tempting distractor, but it supports Dufresne. C also supports her. Only B (night vs midday) can be struck on sight. There is no reversed pair; the student has to map three habitats onto two variables.

II21A-03.note: B is the reversed twin and would support Castellano. A restates the north/south difference that the passage says fits both, and C contradicts it. Same reversed-pair plus known-pattern-pair template as A-01.

II21A-04.note: Drops are Corlan 6, Bexa 9, Dalmi 8, Elsin 13. Dalmi is the binding greenhouse competitor, and Bexa (9) is close and tempting. Farrel is a field variety, so D is struck by category. Test-wise rule: compare against the closest member of the named class.

II21A-05.note: C is the only option that pairs a backswimmer-present pond with an absent one, and the warmer pond (Cobb) has fewer larvae. A, B and D are same-category pairs, so a student who reads the present/absent column strikes them almost on sight. B (16 vs 33, both absent) is the most tempting.

II21A-06.note: Fractions kept are Corvane 0.80, Abrisk 0.75, Eskelin 0.65, Belloway 0.60, Dunmarra 0.50. Abrisk is the closest competitor, but its raw salt mass (45) beats Corvane's 40, so raw-mass readers reject the key. They are drawn to D (Eskelin, lower on both raw figures).

II21B-01.note: A is the reversed twin and would support Grell. The B/D age pair restates or contradicts the age link that fits both accounts. Same template as A-01 and A-03: the key is the cross-site option in the direction of the named hypothesis.

II21B-02.note: C is the reversed twin and would support Hartley. The B/D seasonal pair is the known pattern (D) and its negation (B). Template identical to A-01, A-03 and B-01.

II21B-03.note: A (near the fault) supports Haskins, and B (southern vs northern) fits both accounts. C (tree age) is irrelevant and strikable. The key needs the hollow-collects-CO2 plus hollow-moister link. It is a 'weaken' item with no reversed pair.

II21B-04.note: Specific energies (Wh/kg): prototype 150, H 120, J 140, K 230, L 160. Cell H is sodium-ion, so A is struck by category, and K is visibly higher. L (160) needs one division to reject and is the main lure because its raw figures look large relative to mass.

II21B-05.note: C is the only option naming a white membrane roof. The other three are off-class surfaces with lower values and are struck by matching the surface column alone. Hallam (62) beats Ivy (55), so one comparison covers 'either', but nobody needs that step to find the key.

II21B-06.note: The key needs one station above 1,400 m to be warmer than one below it (Kestow vs Halvern). B (Ilbury warmer than lower Gessel) shows an inversion but entirely within the pool, which makes it the strongest lure. C runs the wrong way, and A sits wholly above the pool.

II21C-01.note: A is the reversed twin and would support Pardo. The B/D old-vs-new pair is the known pattern and its negation. Same dissociation template as A-01, A-03, B-01 and B-02.

II21C-02.note: Mosby vs Renfield holds 'moved' constant and varies distance, so A cuts against 'mainly confusion'. B supports Ortega, C contradicts Moraes, and D fits both. Weakening Ortega only indirectly, through an effect of distance, is a little soft, which is why confidence is medium rather than high.

II21C-03.note: A is the reversed twin and would support Rinaldi. C restates the known pattern and D negates it. Same template again: the reversed pair is on the passage's dissociating sites.

II21C-04.note: Small co-ops raised prices by Neddick 0.55, Pruett 0.45 and Quarles 0.70, so Pruett is binding. Marlow (310 members) is outside the class, and Quarles is the extreme. Neddick is the lure for students who scan only the first small co-op.

II21C-05.note: Standard-method spring scores are 74, 71 and 76, so Redvale is binding. Mercer is a visual-models class (off-class), and Oakhurst is the extreme low. D (Norcott 74) is the remaining lure.

II21C-06.note: Ostler 38 to 17 is the only in-program row that fell below half. Pellow and Marden fail the halving test on sight, and Northby halves but is not in the program, which makes it the only real lure. One row decides it.

II21D-01.note: A is the reversed twin and would support Sandahl. The B/D early-vs-late pair is the known trend and its negation. This is the eighth instance of the same dissociation template.

II21D-02.note: A crosses the two rivers to pit salt without violent floods (lower Sorle) against violent floods without salt (upper Tyrne). B and C compare lower and upper reaches of one river, which fits both claims, and D confounds both factors. The student has to track two rivers on two variables, which makes this a genuinely hard item.

II21D-03.note: D holds storage constant (both dry) and varies iron. B is the strong lure: it involves Wyrlow but is confounded by dampness. A supports Yarrow, and C compares two wooden-beater mills.

II21D-04.note: B holds the decade constant and varies window direction. A is the lure because it varies direction but confounds age. C and D vary only age with the same direction, so they are struck on sight.

II21D-05.note: Tidewater (7,800) is the best-selling installment novel and therefore binding. Vesper Lane is a complete volume (off-class, though closest in value and so the main lure), and Sedge Hollow is the extreme low.

II21D-06.note: Gains for never-Sunday libraries are Tolvane +60, Wexmoor +120 and Zaltby -40, so Wexmoor is binding. Ullerby and Yeovane opened on Sundays (off-class). D (Tolvane, with the higher end figure) lures students who read raw membership instead of gains.
